clue.text: Demure girl sharing male? That's original

indicators.note: the two words share one letter, so the overlapping letter is counted only once

parts.note: demure means prim
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about a shy girl who seems to have something in common with a man.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIM and MARY overlap on their shared M, which 'sharing male' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something primary comes first or is the source, which is what an original thing is.

clue.text: 16 17 briefed estate agent

parts.note: 16 is TRUE, and true means real

indicators.note: briefed means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: 17 is BLUE, the colour of the Conservatives, or Tory

explanation.surface: An estate agent who is a staunch Conservative, briefed on something.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUE BLUE means a loyal Conservative; Tories are the UK's Conservatives, whose colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Realtor is the American word for an estate agent who sells property.

clue.text: Cannibals in Germany and Romania?

parts.note: the names of both countries swallow the word 'man' in their middle, so they literally devour a man

explanation.surface: A question about cannibalism in two European countries.
explanation.walkthrough: GerMANy and RoMANia each contain MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannibals eat human flesh, as do the countries' names, which contain a man.

clue.text: Car wheel, say

definitions.meaning: a wheel is an example of something that rolls along

explanation.surface: A car wheel offered as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rolls-Royce is nicknamed this in British slang, and a wheel is a cylinder that rolls.

clue.text: Standard disguises

definitions.meaning: a regiment's flag or banner, as in 'troop the colour'
false appearances, as in sailing under false ...

explanation.surface: Two bare words suggesting that norms are a kind of mask.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's flag is its colours, and a pretence or false show is also called colours.

clue.text: Balls developed, then got too big

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls
developed means grew

explanation.surface: Something rounded matured and became too large.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To overgrow is to grow beyond the right size, so it got too big.

clue.text: Fabric in 31, covering left leg

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: 31 is YELLOW, and or is gold or yellow in heraldry
on is the leg side of the cricket field

explanation.surface: A fabric in yellow covers someone's left leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlon is a trade name for an acrylic fibre used in knitwear fabric.

clue.text: Old railwaymen climbing ladder

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, back to front

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, now defunct

explanation.surface: Retired railway workers going up a ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladder' is the snag in tights or stockings, not a thing to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A run in stockings is a ladder, a line of unravelled stitches.

clue.text: Part of male personality lost in a drummer

parts.note: in Jung's psychology the anima is the feminine side of a man's psyche
L is the abbreviation for lost, as in sports tables

explanation.surface: A drummer has lost part of his masculine personality.
explanation.walkthrough: Animal is the wild drummer of the Muppets.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal is the frenzied drummer in the Muppets' band, the Electric Mayhem.

clue.text: Sexual relationship beginning in Venetian thoroughfare?

indicators.note: one piece is set inside the other here

parts.note: the streets of Venice are canals

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A romance starting on a canal in Venice, the city of lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' takes the R of relationship, and 'in' puts it inside CANAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnal means of the flesh, bodily, so sexual in the physical sense.

clue.text: Must have fish? That's annoying

parts.note: something you must have is a need
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone irritated by a companion's insistence on ordering fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Needling someone is provoking or irritating them with repeated jibes.

clue.text: String of bloomers in article from French newspaper

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article
the i is a British daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece about a string of embarrassing blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like mistakes or underwear but means flowers; the i is a UK newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hawaiian garland is a string of flowers, and bloomers are flowering plants.

clue.text: Faster-working machine-gun

indicators.note: letters at work are being rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An upgraded machine gun that fires more quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges FASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: One of the 16 1 5 in which old woman seduces a man

indicators.note: to seduce is to take someone in, so the man is taken inside the other pieces

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A seduction scene in which an older woman wins over a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 1 5 refers to the three linked lights TRUE, PRIMARY and COLOURS; 'seduces' signals taking the man in.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is one of the three subtractive primary colours used in printing, with cyan and yellow.

clue.text: Triumphant expression from husband in Carmen?

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: read as car men, the AA, the British motoring organisation with roadside patrolmen

explanation.surface: A cry of triumph from the husband in Bizet's opera Carmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carmen' is read as 'car men', the patrolmen of the AA, Britain's Automobile Association.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of triumph or discovery, said when someone catches you out.

clue.text: See 30
Fly down to Winchester?

parts.note: feeling down is feeling blue
a winchester is a large bottle, used for chemicals or wine

explanation.surface: Instructions to fly down to the cathedral city of Winchester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb of travel, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluebottle is a common blowfly with a metallic blue body.

clue.text: Fancy a new fence in one of the 16 1 5

indicators.note: the letters are enclosed within the words, like a field fenced in

explanation.surface: Someone fancies building a new fence painted in a primary colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 1 5 are TRUE PRIMARY COLOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan, a greenish blue, is one of the three subtractive primary colours alongside magenta and yellow.

clue.text: Labour leader almost a Green inside? Well, I'll be blowed!

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
almost means without the last letter

parts.note: Jeremy Corbyn led the UK Labour Party
lime is a shade of green

explanation.surface: Surprise that the Labour leader is almost a Green Party member at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Corbyn led Britain's Labour Party from 2015 to 2020. 'almost' cuts the N, and 'inside' puts LIME within CORBY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British exclamations of astonishment, the first a corruption of 'God blind me'.

clue.text: Turned originators of Rock Against Racism off including opener from Chuck Berry

indicators.note: the letters have gone off, spoiled and out of order
originators are the starting letters of each word
an opener is the first letter

explanation.surface: Organisers of the Rock Against Racism concerts turned someone away, even with a Chuck Berry song.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock Against Racism was a 1970s British concert campaign. 'Chuck Berry' looks like one name, but 'Berry' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The redcurrant is a small, sharp red fruit growing in clusters on a bush.

clue.text: Leader touring around Washington State

indicators.note: touring means going around, so one piece encloses the other
around signals the letters being turned about into a new order

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: A leader on a tour around Washington State.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges the clue's first word into DELARE, which 'touring' puts round the state code. 'Washington State' looks like one name, but 'State' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is a US state, the first to ratify the Constitution.

clue.text: Deal possibly avoiding day in court

indicators.note: avoiding something means leaving it out

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber, an example of wood

explanation.surface: A plea bargain struck so that someone does not have to spend a day in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to woo them, seeking their affection.

clue.text: Love of the French lyric poems

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
des is French for 'of the' in the plural

explanation.surface: A description of French love poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, often addressed to a subject in an elevated style.

clue.text: Short chap taking short cut

indicators.note: short means losing the last letter

parts.note: to dock is to cut, as with a tail

explanation.surface: A small man taking a shortcut.
explanation.walkthrough: Doc is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White.
explanation.definitionFit: Doc is one of the seven dwarfs, so a short fellow.

clue.text: Banker model bedded after strip shows

indicators.note: stripping the outer letters off the words shows what is hidden inside

explanation.surface: A financier sleeps with a model after a strip show.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a 'banker' can be a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elbe is a major river in central Europe, and a river is something with banks.

clue.text: See 17
Cast part in Spellbound

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould anew, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as the letters to be rearranged; that these letters also run backwards across 'Cast part' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: An actor is cast in a role in Hitchcock's film Spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' rearranges PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rapt is completely absorbed or entranced, held as if by a spell.

clue.text: Found small number in support

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
one is a small number

explanation.surface: A small number found inside a support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' is the verb to establish, not the past of find.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer something is to establish it first, to found it.

clue.text: Henry Percy developed a secret code

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters change order

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry Percy, the Hotspur of history, developed a secret code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges H plus PERCY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cypher, also spelt cipher, is a secret way of writing a message.

clue.text: See 19
After eating half of yogurt, backing singer surprisingly hits right note

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
surprisingly signals letters coming out in an unexpected order
backing means reading the letters backwards
half of the word, here its last three letters

explanation.surface: A backing singer eats a yogurt and then surprises everyone by singing in tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes the back three letters of yogurt and 'backing' turns them round; 'surprisingly' rearranges the singer into RINGSE, which takes them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rings true sounds convincing, like a note struck correctly.

clue.text: Footballer lacking 25 perhaps, as a flier

parts.note: 25 is BOTTLE, slang for courage; lacking it is being cowardly
the Hammers are West Ham United, a London football club

explanation.surface: A footballer without courage is compared to something flighty.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham United's players are called the Hammers.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellowhammer is a bunting with a bright yellow head, so a bird that flies.

clue.text: Kill time at work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An instruction to pass the hours at the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kill time' looks like one phrase; 'Kill' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is slang for killing them, especially by hanging or as a suicide.

clue.text: Private hospital in towering civic building

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: towering means very tall
something private is your own

explanation.surface: A private hospital housed in a towering municipal building.
explanation.definitionFit: A town hall houses a local council's offices, so it is a civic building.

clue.text: Eggs are done, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the words are spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: things that are done are over

explanation.surface: Someone announces that the eggs are cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the Latin plural for egg cells.

clue.text: See 31
One who managed to treat a lisp? Yes, mostly

indicators.note: to treat something is to work on it, so the letters are reworked
mostly means all but the last letter

explanation.surface: A speech therapist curing a lisp, with a hesitant mostly-yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the S of Yes; 'treat' rearranges A LISP plus YE. Bob Paisley managed Liverpool FC.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Paisley was a famous football manager, winning several European Cups with Liverpool.

clue.text: Make fun of European recipe involving rare English cheese

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to guy someone is to ridicule them
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Mocking a continental recipe that uses a rare English cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts the R for rare inside GUY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruyère is a hard Swiss cheese named after a district in Fribourg.
